findings.note: Quadratic append. prepareAppend (internal/fsm/run/store.go:130-166) recounts the counted-event total by walking every previously stored line and JSON-probing each one via lineType (store.go:171-178), and jsonlStore.Append (internal/fsm/run/store_jsonl.go:224-233) re-reads and re-splits the whole audit file on every single append. Recording n events is therefore O(n^2) in both file I/O and JSON parsing. With DefaultMaxEvents = 100000 (types.go) and MaxLine = 1MB, a long run pays this on every step, and the cost is paid while holding the run lock. The counted total is derivable incrementally (FoldState already threads through Append), so the rescan is avoidable.

findings.note: Double-quoted run id in the error message. internal/fsm/run/types.go:371 formats with %q an argument that is already strconv.Quote(id), so an invalid id surfaces to the user as: invalid run id "\"mrv-bad\"". This error reaches the CLI through internal/fsm/cli/run.go:898 and internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:222/228, so it is user-visible. Drop the strconv.Quote (and the strconv import if it becomes unused).

summarize (internal/fsm/run/store.go:192-197) returns on the parse error before assigning s.Torn, which is only set at line 198. EventsWithLines does set Log.Torn even when parseLines fails, so the information is available — but a run that is BOTH torn and chain-broken is listed with Torn=false. That hides the one remedy the operator has (RepairTail) behind a chain error that looks unrecoverable. Set s.Torn from the log before the error return.

evidence.note: if err != nil { s.Error = err.Error(); return s } precedes s.Torn = log.Torn != nil

findings.note: Inconsistent JSON strictness on the same stored line. parseLines uses a json.Decoder (internal/fsm/run/store.go:94), which decodes the first value and silently ignores any trailing bytes on the line, while lineType uses json.Unmarshal (store.go:175), which rejects them. A line carrying trailing bytes therefore decodes as a valid chained event but reports type "", so it is not countedType and escapes the MaxEvents cap entirely. The hash chain does detect such a line at the next append (CAS on ChainHead) or at the next line's Prev check, which keeps this out of medium severity, but the audit reader should be the strict one: use json.Unmarshal in parseLines so both paths agree on what a well-formed line is.

evidence.note: dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(line)) — trailing bytes after the first value are not rejected
lineType uses json.Unmarshal, which does reject trailing bytes, yielding type ""
